clusters.neutral_headline: She gets 16 pelvic exams a day – so yours don’t hurt

items.title: She gets 16 pelvic exams a day – so yours don’t hurt
items.standfirst: Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast examsOn her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina. She works full-time as a gynecological teaching assistant (GTA) – a layperson who helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams before they work with actual patients.It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. Contrary to common belief, pap smears – tests that screen for cervical cancer – don’t have to be painful. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Never thought I’d eat that’: how vegetable prescriptions are helping Britons with diabetes
items.standfirst: WellFed participants in Cornwall report better blood sugar levels with help of free veg boxes, cooking and gardeningThe participants admitted that throughout their life, their food choices had been far from ideal: egg and chips, hearty roasts, raw fry – a Cornish one-pan dish of bacon, potatoes and onions, often fried in lard and once beloved of miners and fishers.But here they were, at a community orchard in the harbourside town of St Ives in south-west Cornwall, massaging Swiss chard (to soften the leaves), dicing carrots, adding lentils into a pot to create a low-GI, high-fibre – and tasty – shepherd’s bake.
